extracted.intended_audience: State Exchange officials and regulators (FFE States), State plan-management staff, and QHP issuers submitting certification data
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the proposed regulatory criteria for (1) when an FFE State may conduct its own provider access/network adequacy reviews and ECP certification reviews, and (2) issuer requirements for ECP thresholds and ECP data/reporting in QHP certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network plans must include ECPs and adequate provider types (§155.1050(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: An FFE State with an Effective Provider Access Review Program would be required to ensure that a QHP issuer that uses a network of providers ensures that its network of providers, as available to all enrollees, includes ECPs in accordance with §156.235, and maintains a network that is sufficient in number and types of providers, including providers that specialize in mental health and substance use disorder services, to ensure that all services will be accessible without unreasonable delay, and is consistent with the rules for network plans of section 2702(c) of the PHS Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This criterion requires networks to include eligible ECPs and adequate specialty coverage (e.g., mental health/SUD). It ties network sufficiency to timeliness of access and statutory provisions; HHS would evaluate whether State-level reviews ensure these elements are present when deferring reviews to States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-network plans must provide sufficient choice accepting payment in full (§155.1050(d)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: An FFE State with an Effective Provider Access Review Program must ensure that a QHP issuer that does not use a network of providers (a non-network plan) provides access to a sufficient choice of providers that accept the non-network plan's benefit amount as payment in full, including ECPs and providers that specialize in mental health and substance use disorder services, to ensure that all services will be accessible without unreasonable delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations of non-network plans focus on demonstrated provider choice and whether providers accept the issuer's benefit amount as payment in full. States must have processes to collect evidence showing provider availability and acceptance of payment amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: State provider access standards established in statute/regulation and reporting of delegation (§155.1050(d)(4)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The FFE State has established provider access standards that are set forth in State statute or regulation which are consistent with provider access standards as set forth in §156.230(a)(1)(ii) and (iii), and reports to HHS whether the State has delegated authority to some entity other than the State Department of Insurance to perform any or all provider access review activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion assesses whether the State's legal authority and formal standards exist and align with federal expectations, and requires transparency about any delegation of review authority to non-DOI entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting systems, metrics, and methodology documentation (§155.1050(d)(4)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The FFE State's provider access review process includes reporting systems for State-required provider access metrics and documentation of methodology and the State provides descriptions of all data collection systems, resources, templates, and methodologies used by the State or the State's delegated entity to collect and review provider access data; and the State receives from issuers data and documentation in connection with provider access standards that are sufficient to conduct the examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators will look for concrete reporting systems, defined metrics, and clear methodological documentation (data systems, templates, validation methods). The State must demonstrate it obtains sufficient issuer-submitted data to perform reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures to ensure compliance and enforcement frameworks (§155.1050(d)(4)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The FFE State's provider access review process includes procedures to ensure full and ongoing compliance with State provider access standards and enforcement frameworks applicable to issuers that fail to meet provider access standards so that those issuers come into compliance with State provider access standards, including standardized processes to assess efforts the issuer is pursuing to come into compliance with State provider access standards, and implementing any justification and exception processes for issuers that have not yet or cannot meet provider access requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State processes must include enforcement mechanisms, standardized assessment of issuer remediation efforts, and documented exception/justification handling. HHS will expect evidence that noncompliant issuers are identified and brought into compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear procedures and timelines for regular provider access reviews (§155.1050(d)(4)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: The FFE State establishes and maintains clear procedures and timeline requirements for regular provider access reviews, including processes that ensure reviews occur prior to each plan year's QHP certification cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews must be routine and scheduled (not only reactive); timely completion prior to QHP certification is required. States should document timelines and workflows for performing reviews within the certification cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process for consumer-related provider access complaints (§155.1050(d)(4)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: The FFE State has a process for monitoring and addressing consumer-related provider access complaints to ensure sufficient access to providers consistent with section 1311(c)(1)(B) of the Affordable Care Act and as set forth in State statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must track and respond to consumer complaints about provider access (e.g., directory inaccuracies, appointment availability) and incorporate complaint monitoring into adequacy assessments and corrective actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process to collect/review information on non-network plan access (§155.1050(d)(4)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: The FFE State has a process to collect and review information sufficient to show that non-network plans provide access to a sufficient choice of providers that accept the non-network plan's benefit amount as payment in full.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must demonstrate data collection and review protocols specific to non-network plans (provider lists, payment acceptance verification) to show adequate access.

rubrics_metrics.name: State must demonstrate criteria for both network and non-network plans
rubrics_metrics.description: A State would need to demonstrate that it meets applicable criteria for both network plans and non-network plans under §155.1050(d), if they decide to certify such plans; a State would not be permitted to elect to conduct provider access certification reviews for only network plans and not non-network plans, if they certify such plans, or vice versa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS requires comprehensive capacity across both plan types when States seek authority to perform certification reviews for an issuer offering both types; this prevents splitting review authority across entities and promotes consistent methodologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHS determination, exceptions, notification, and reevaluation process (§155.1050(d)(5)-(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS would determine whether a State has an Effective Provider Access Review Program based on information available that demonstrates whether the program meets the criteria; HHS may grant exceptions if in the interests of qualified individuals; HHS would notify the FFE State in writing of its decision regarding whether the State is determined to have an Effective Provider Access Review Program and would reserve the right at any time to evaluate whether circumstances have changed such that it has established, or no longer has, an Effective Provider Access Review Program, potentially resulting in HHS assuming or transitioning responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes the evaluative and oversight process: HHS uses available information, can make case-by-case exceptions, provides written findings, and may reassess/withdraw delegation. States should be prepared for periodic and ad hoc HHS evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation of federal time/distance and appointment wait time standards to HHS-conducted reviews (§156.230(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Revising §156.230(a)(2)(i) and (ii) to clarify that requirements to meet time and distance standards and appointment wait time standards at §156.230(a)(2) only apply to States that HHS has determined do not satisfy the criteria to be considered to have an Effective Provider Access Review Program or that do not elect to conduct their own provider access reviews of issuers as described at proposed new §155.1050(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When HHS defers reviews to an Effective State program, these specific quantitative time/distance/appointment wait requirements would not be imposed by HHS; they remain applicable where HHS itself conducts reviews or for States lacking delegated Effective status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory changes clarifying when §156.230 standards apply
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed amendments to §156.230 include (1) revising the heading to 'Provider access standards for network plans'; (2) removing the requirement that a QHP must use a provider network and clarifying that the standards described apply to a QHP that uses a network of providers; (3) revising exceptions to apply only when HHS is conducting network adequacy reviews; and (4) conforming revisions to other paragraphs to reflect delegation to FFE States that demonstrate sufficient authority and technical capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These regulatory edits change which standards are HHS-imposed versus state-determined and are relevant to how adequacy reviews are scoped depending on whether HHS or a State conducts the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: ECP minimum percentage (threshold) requirements reduced from 35% to 20% (§156.235)
rubrics_metrics.description: To reduce administrative burden, proposed reduction of the overall ECP threshold, FQHC threshold, and family planning provider threshold requirements from 35 percent to 20 percent for both medical QHP and SADP issuers in FFE States, including States performing plan management, beginning PY 2027; SADP FQHC threshold likewise set at 20 percent for FQHCs offering dental services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuers are considered to meet the ECP standard if they contract with at least 20% of available ECPs (and separately 20% of available FQHCs and family planning providers) in each plan's service area. Calculation methodology follows prior years. Issuers may exceed the minimum; HHS will monitor access impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting multiple providers at a single location as one ECP for threshold calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of satisfying the minimum percentage requirement (the ECP threshold), multiple providers at a single location count as a single ECP toward both the available ECPs in the plan's service area and the contracted ECPs included in the issuer's network for calculating the threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies denominator/numerator counting rules for threshold calculations and affects how issuers and States compute percentage satisfaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replace narrative justification with contract negotiation status reporting via MPMS ECP UI (§156.235(a)(3)/(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify regulatory language so that an issuer include as part of its QHP application the status of contract offers to qualified ECPs available in the network plan's service area (collected via the ECP UI in MPMS), removing the open-ended narrative justification previously required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPMS ECP UI collects standardized contract negotiation statuses (e.g., executed, offer made awaiting response, not offered due to no response). HHS finds this information sufficient in lieu of narrative explanations and will rely on it for ECP certification reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to report contract status at least for ECPs included or offered in the issuer's network
rubrics_metrics.description: Issuers are not required to designate the contract negotiation status for all available ECPs in their QHP application; they must at least report on the status of contract offers for all ECPs which the issuer has either included in its network plan or offered a contract to be included in its network plan within each service area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limits issuer reporting burden while ensuring HHS/States receive status information for ECPs relevant to the issuer's network or active contracting efforts. Different status selections have different credit implications for thresholds and category/county requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for an Effective ECP Review Program (state eligibility to conduct ECP certification reviews) (§155.1051)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning PY 2027, FFE States (including States performing plan management) may elect to conduct their own ECP certification reviews of QHP issuers' plans provided the State demonstrates it has sufficient authority and the technical capacity to conduct these reviews by satisfying applicable criteria established by HHS to be considered an Effective ECP Review Program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS will assess State legal authority to enforce ECP-related certification criteria, technical means to conduct assessments (data systems, methodologies), and enforcement capability. States with prior experience or plan-management functions may be more likely to qualify; HHS may set specific documentation requirements similar to provider access review criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ECP UI / MPMS data and contract status for ECP certification reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS uses standardized ECP data obtained through MPMS (ECP UI) — including which qualified ECPs have executed contracts, contract negotiation statuses, and related data — to perform ECP certification reviews and to calculate satisfaction of the ECP standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States or HHS conducting ECP reviews will rely on the structured MPMS data rather than narrative submissions; contract negotiation statuses influence credit toward thresholds and category/county/Indian health care requirements. The ECP UI is intended to reduce issuer burden and standardize review inputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHS support resources to States for network adequacy/ECP reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS would provide numerous resources to States to utilize as they develop and enhance their network adequacy review capabilities — including a network adequacy template, other supporting document templates, manual data validation resources, and FAQs — and make available extensive resources originally developed for Federal network adequacy review during the annual QHP certification cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability of templates, validation tools, and FAQs is part of the proposed approach to help States build capacity. States seeking delegation should plan to leverage these HHS-provided resources when implementing or documenting their review processes.
